sanskrit: tatas tu rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā hanūmatākṣe nihate kumāre manaḥ samādhāya tadendrakalpaṃ samādideśendrajitaṃ sa roṣāt
english: Then the great-souled lord of rākṣasas, having steadied his mind on learning that young Akṣa had been slain by Hanumān, in wrath dispatched Indrajit, who resembled Indra himself.

sanskrit: tvam astravic chastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ surāsurāṇām api śokadātā sureṣu sendreṣu ca dṛṣṭakarmā pitāmahārādhanasaṃcitāstraḥ
english: "You are the foremost among those who bear weapons, the master of missile-lore, who has brought grief to gods and asuras alike; your valor is proven against the gods along with Indra, and your arsenal of weapons has been accumulated through worship of the Grandsire."

sanskrit: tavāstrabalam āsādya nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ na kaś cit triṣu lokeṣu saṃyuge na gataśramaḥ
english: "When confronted with the force of your missiles, neither asuras nor the Marut hosts — indeed no one in the three worlds — has ever come away unwearied in battle."

sanskrit: bhujavīryābhiguptaś ca tapasā cābhirakṣitaḥ deśakālavibhāgajñas tvam eva matisattamaḥ
english: "Protected by the might of your arms and shielded by your austerities, knowing the distinction of time and place — you alone are the best in wisdom."

sanskrit: na te 'sty aśakyaṃ samareṣu karmaṇā na te 'sty akāryaṃ matipūrvamantraṇe na so 'sti kaś cit triṣu saṃgraheṣu vai na veda yas te 'strabalaṃ balaṃ ca te
english: "There is no feat impossible for you in battle, no counsel beyond your deliberate wisdom; there is no one in the three conflicts who does not know your missile-strength and your prowess."

sanskrit: mamānurūpaṃ tapaso balaṃ ca te parākramaś cāstrabalaṃ ca saṃyuge na tvāṃ samāsādya raṇāvamarde manaḥ śramaṃ gacchati niścitārtham
english: "Your austerity, strength, valor, and missile-might in battle are a fitting match for mine; the mind of one who faces you in the press of war finds no room for fatigue — this is certain."

sanskrit: nihatā iṃkarāḥ sarve jambumālī ca rākṣasaḥ amātyaputrā vīrāś ca pañca senāgrayāyinaḥ
english: "Slain are all the commanders, the rākṣasa Jambumālī, and the five heroic sons of ministers who led the vanguard of the army."

sanskrit: sahodaras te dayitaḥ kumāro 'kṣaś ca sūditaḥ na tu teṣv eva me sāro yas tvayy ariniṣūdana
english: "Your beloved younger brother, the prince Akṣa, has also been killed; yet I place no great stock in those losses, O slayer of enemies — for you remain."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā matiman mahad balaṃ kapeḥ prabhāvaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca tvam ātmanaś cāpi samīkṣya sāraṃ kuruṣva vegaṃ svabalānurūpam
english: "Having now seen this great might of the monkey, his power and valor, and having also measured your own essential strength, O wise one, marshal your speed in keeping with your own force."

sanskrit: balāvamardas tvayi saṃnikṛṣṭe yathā gate śāmyati śāntaśatrau tathā samīkṣyātmabalaṃ paraṃ ca samārabhasvāstravidāṃ variṣṭha
english: "As the trampling of one's force subsides when you draw near, just as it ceases when the foe is quelled — weighing your own power against the enemy's, engage now, O foremost among masters of missiles."

sanskrit: na khalv iyaṃ matiḥ śreṣṭhā yat tvāṃ saṃpreṣayāmy aham iyaṃ ca rājadharmāṇāṃ kṣatrasya ca matir matā
english: "This is certainly not the highest counsel — that I send you forth; yet this is the considered course recognized for kingly duty and for the Kṣatriya code."

sanskrit: nānāśastraiś ca saṃgrāme vaiśāradyam ariṃdama avaśyam eva boddhavyaṃ kāmyaś ca vijayo raṇe
english: "The proficiency in battle with manifold weapons must certainly be employed, O subduer of enemies, and victory in war is to be desired."

sanskrit: tataḥ pitus tad vacanaṃ niśamya pradakṣiṇaṃ dakṣasutaprabhāvaḥ cakāra bhartāram adīnasattvo raṇāya vīraḥ pratipannabuddhiḥ
english: Then, having heard his father's words, that hero of unwaning spirit — possessing the prowess of Dakṣa's son — circumambulated his lord, resolved in mind for battle.

sanskrit: tatas taiḥ svagaṇair iṣṭair indrajit pratipūjitaḥ yuddhoddhatakṛtotsāhaḥ saṃgrāmaṃ pratipadyata
english: Then Indrajit, duly honored by his own dear companions, his martial enthusiasm roused for combat, set out for the battlefield.

sanskrit: śrīmān padmapalāśākṣo rākṣasādhipateḥ sutaḥ nirjagāma mahātejāḥ samudra iva parvasu
english: The glorious son of the lord of rākṣasas, lotus-petal-eyed, of great splendor, sallied forth like the ocean at the full moon.

sanskrit: sa pakṣi rājopamatulyavegair vyālaiś caturbhiḥ sitatīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraiḥ rathaṃ samāyuktam asaṃgavegaṃ samārurohendrajid indrakalpaḥ
english: Indrajit, resembling Indra, mounted a chariot harnessed with four serpents whose speed equaled that of the king of birds, whose fangs were white and sharp, and whose swiftness was unimpeded.

sanskrit: sa rathī dhanvināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ śastrajño 'stravidāṃ varaḥ rathenābhiyayau kṣipraṃ hanūmān yatra so 'bhavat
english: That chariot-warrior, foremost of archers, expert in weapons, and best among masters of missiles, swiftly rode in his chariot to where Hanumān stood.

sanskrit: sa tasya rathanirghoṣaṃ jyāsvanaṃ kārmukasya ca niśamya harivīro 'sau saṃprahṛṣṭataro 'bhavat
english: That hero of the monkeys, hearing the rumble of his chariot and the twang of his bow, became all the more elated.

sanskrit: sumahac cāpam ādāya śitaśalyāṃś ca sāyakān hanūmantam abhipretya jagāma raṇapaṇḍitaḥ
english: Taking up his great bow and sharp-pointed arrows, the expert in battle advanced toward Hanumān with clear intent.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tataḥ saṃyati jātaharṣe raṇāya nirgacchati bāṇapāṇau diśaś ca sarvāḥ kaluṣā babhūvur mṛgāś ca raudrā bahudhā vineduḥ
english: As he, arrow in hand, set forth for battle with heightened exultation, all the directions turned turbid and fearsome beasts cried out in many voices.

sanskrit: samāgatās tatra tu nāgayakṣā maharṣayaś cakracarāś ca siddhāḥ nabhaḥ samāvṛtya ca pakṣisaṃghā vinedur uccaiḥ paramaprahṛṣṭāḥ
english: Nāgas and Yakṣas, great sages, and Siddhas moving in circles gathered there; flocks of birds filled the sky and cried out aloud, supremely excited.

sanskrit: āyantaṃ sarathaṃ dṛṣṭvā tūrṇam indrajitaṃ kapiḥ vinanāda mahānādaṃ vyavardhata ca vegavān
english: Seeing Indrajit approaching swiftly with his chariot, the swift monkey let out a mighty roar and grew in stature.

sanskrit: indrajit tu rathaṃ divyam āsthitaś citrakārmukaḥ dhanur visphārayām āsa taḍidūrjitaniḥsvanam
english: Indrajit, mounted on his divine chariot with his variegated bow, twanged his bow with a sound as mighty as a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tataḥ sametāv atitīkṣṇavegau mahābalau tau raṇanirviśaṅkau kapiś ca rakṣo'dhipateś ca putraḥ surāsurendrāv iva baddhavairau
english: Then those two, of exceedingly sharp speed and great strength, fearless in battle — the monkey and the son of the rākṣasa lord — came together, like the kings of gods and asuras locked in enmity.

sanskrit: sa tasya vīrasya mahārathasyā dhanuṣmataḥ saṃyati saṃmatasya śarapravegaṃ vyahanat pravṛddhaś cacāra mārge pitur aprameyaḥ
english: The immeasurable monkey, grown mighty, deflected the swift rush of arrows of that heroic great-chariot warrior renowned on the battlefield, and ranged about in the path of combat — himself beyond measure, surpassing his father's expectations.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarān āyatatīkṣṇaśalyān supatriṇaḥ kāñcanacitrapuṅkhān mumoca vīraḥ paravīrahantā susaṃtatān vajranipātavegān
english: Then that hero, slayer of enemy champions, released arrows with long, sharp heads, well-feathered, with gilded colorful nocks, shot in rapid succession with the speed of a falling thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sa tasya tat syandananiḥsvanaṃ ca mṛdaṅgabherīpaṭahasvanaṃ ca vikṛṣyamāṇasya ca kārmukasya niśamya ghoṣaṃ punar utpapāta
english: Hearing the rumble of his chariot, the sound of kettledrums, war-drums, and battle-drums, and the twang of the straining bow, he leapt into the air again.

sanskrit: śarāṇām antareṣv āśu vyavartata mahākapiḥ haris tasyābhilakṣasya mokṣayaṃl lakṣyasaṃgraham
english: The great monkey swiftly dodged between the arrows, eluding that adversary's targeting, foiling his aim's concentration.

sanskrit: śarāṇām agratas tasya punaḥ samabhivartata prasārya hastau hanumān utpapātānilātmajaḥ
english: Spreading out his hands, Hanumān, son of the Wind, again darted forward in front of those arrows and leapt aloft.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau vegasaṃpannau raṇakarmaviśāradau sarvabhūtamanogrāhi cakratur yuddham uttamam
english: Those two, both endowed with speed and skilled in the arts of war, waged an incomparable battle that captivated the minds of all living beings.

sanskrit: hanūmato veda na rākṣaso 'ntaraṃ na mārutis tasya mahātmano 'ntaram parasparaṃ nirviṣahau babhūvatuḥ sametya tau devasamānavikramau
english: The rākṣasa could find no opening in Hanumān, nor could Māruti find an opening in that great-souled one; coming together, those two of valor equal to the gods found each other mutually irresistible.

sanskrit: tatas tu lakṣye sa vihanyamāne śareṣu mogheṣu ca saṃpatatsu jagāma cintāṃ mahatīṃ mahātmā samādhisaṃyogasamāhitātmā
english: Then, as his mark was missed and his arrows fell in vain, that great-souled one fell into deep deliberation, his mind composed in contemplative concentration.

sanskrit: tato matiṃ rākṣasarājasūnuś cakāra tasmin harivīramukhye avadhyatāṃ tasya kapeḥ samīkṣya kathaṃ nigacched iti nigrahārtham
english: Then the son of the rākṣasa king formed a resolve regarding that foremost monkey hero — recognizing the monkey's invincibility, how might he be restrained — for the purpose of his capture.

sanskrit: tataḥ paitāmahāṃ vīraḥ so 'stram astravidāṃ varaḥ saṃdadhe sumahātejās taṃ haripravaraṃ prati
english: Then that hero of immense splendor, best among masters of missiles, trained the Paitāmaha weapon — the missile of the Grandsire — upon that foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: avadhyo 'yam iti jñātvā tam astreṇāstratattvavit nijagrāha mahābāhur mārutātmajam indrajit
english: Knowing this one to be inviolable, the long-armed Indrajit, conversant with the true nature of missiles, bound the son of the Wind-god with that weapon.

sanskrit: tena baddhas tato 'streṇa rākṣasena sa vānaraḥ abhavan nirviceṣṭaś ca papāta ca mahītale
english: Bound by that weapon of the rākṣasa, the monkey became motionless and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tato 'tha buddhvā sa tadāstrabandhaṃ prabhoḥ prabhāvād vigatālpavegaḥ pitāmahānugraham ātmanaś ca vicintayām āsa haripravīraḥ
english: Then that foremost monkey hero, having recognized the missile's binding through the power of its master, his lesser speed having departed, reflected on the Grandsire's boon and on his own situation.

sanskrit: tataḥ svāyambhuvair mantrair brahmāstram abhimantritam hanūmāṃś cintayām āsa varadānaṃ pitāmahāt
english: Then Hanumān contemplated the Brahma-weapon enchanted with the spells of Svāyambhuva, and the boon he had received from the Grandsire.

sanskrit: na me 'strabandhasya ca śaktir asti vimokṣaṇe lokaguroḥ prabhāvāt ity evam evaṃvihito 'strabandho mayātmayoner anuvartitavyaḥ
english: "I have no power to release myself from this missile-bondage, for it comes from the power of the world's preceptor; thus this missile-bondage, being of such a nature, must be honored by me, the son born of the self-existent."

sanskrit: sa vīryam astrasya kapir vicārya pitāmahānugraham ātmanaś ca vimokṣaśaktiṃ paricintayitvā pitāmahājñām anuvartate sma
english: The monkey, having considered the power of the missile and his own capacity for release, and having reflected on the Grandsire's grace, abided by the Grandsire's command.

sanskrit: astreṇāpi hi baddhasya bhayaṃ mama na jāyate pitāmahamahendrābhyāṃ rakṣitasyānilena ca
english: "Even bound by the missile, no fear arises in me, for I am protected by the Grandsire, by Mahendra, and by the Wind-god."

sanskrit: grahaṇe cāpi rakṣobhir mahan me guṇadarśanam rākṣasendreṇa saṃvādas tasmād gṛhṇantu māṃ pare
english: "Moreover, in being captured by the rākṣasas I see a great advantage — a conversation with the king of rākṣasas; let the enemies therefore take me."

sanskrit: sa niścitārthaḥ paravīrahantā samīkṣya karī vinivṛttaceṣṭaḥ paraiḥ prasahyābhigatair nigṛhya nanāda tais taiḥ paribhartsyamānaḥ
english: His purpose settled — that slayer of enemy heroes — having considered it like a wise elephant, ceased his efforts; restrained by enemies who pressed upon him by force, he roared while being reviled by them with various insults.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ rākṣasā dṛṣṭvā nirviceṣṭam ariṃdamam babandhuḥ śaṇavalkaiś ca drumacīraiś ca saṃhataiḥ
english: Then the rākṣasas, seeing that subduer of enemies motionless, bound him with cords of hemp and with strips of bark from trees twisted together.

sanskrit: sa rocayām āsa paraiś ca bandhanaṃ prasahya vīrair abhinigrahaṃ ca kautūhalān māṃ yadi rākṣasendro draṣṭuṃ vyavasyed iti niścitārthaḥ
english: He approved of this binding and forcible capture by the enemy warriors, his purpose resolved, out of curiosity — thinking, "If only the lord of rākṣasas might decide to see me."

sanskrit: sa baddhas tena valkena vimukto 'streṇa vīryavān astrabandhaḥ sa cānyaṃ hi na bandham anuvartate
english: Bound by that bark cord, he was in fact released by the missile — for the powerful missile-bond does not accompany any other bond.

sanskrit: athendrajit taṃ drumacīrabandhaṃ vicārya vīraḥ kapisattamaṃ tam vimuktam astreṇa jagāma cintām anyena baddho hy anuvartate 'stram
english: Then Indrajit the hero, reflecting on that bark-cord binding of that foremost monkey who had been freed from the missile-bond, fell into worry — for one bound by another bond does not remain under the missile's hold.

sanskrit: aho mahat karma kṛtaṃ nirarthakaṃ na rākṣasair mantragatir vimṛṣṭā punaś ca nāstre vihate 'stram anyat pravartate saṃśayitāḥ sma sarve
english: "Alas, a great deed has been done to no purpose! The rākṣasas did not reflect on the lore of missiles; moreover, when one missile is deployed, no other missile can operate — we are all in doubt."

sanskrit: astreṇa hanumān mukto nātmānam avabudhyate kṛṣyamāṇas tu rakṣobhis taiś ca bandhair nipīḍitaḥ
english: Hanumān, freed by the missile, did not realize his own liberation, being dragged by the rākṣasas and oppressed by those bonds.

sanskrit: hanyamānas tataḥ krūrai rākṣasaiḥ kāṣṭhamuṣṭibhiḥ samīpaṃ rākṣasendrasya prākṛṣyata sa vānaraḥ
english: Then the monkey, beaten by the cruel rākṣasas with fists and wooden clubs, was dragged to the presence of the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: athendrajit taṃ prasamīkṣya muktam astreṇa baddhaṃ drumacīrasūtraiḥ vyadarśayat tatra mahābalaṃ taṃ haripravīraṃ sagaṇāya rājñe
english: Then Indrajit, closely observing him freed from the missile but bound with bark-cord ropes, presented that immensely powerful monkey hero to the king before his assembled retinue.

sanskrit: taṃ mattam iva mātaṅgaṃ baddhaṃ kapivarottamam rākṣasā rākṣasendrāya rāvaṇāya nyavedayan
english: The rākṣasas presented that bound foremost-of-monkeys, like a maddened elephant in bonds, to Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: ko 'yaṃ kasya kuto vāpi kiṃ kāryaṃ ko vyapāśrayaḥ iti rākṣasavīrāṇāṃ tatra saṃjajñire kathāḥ
english: "Who is this? Whose is he? Where does he come from? What is his purpose? What is his recourse?" — such discussions arose among the rākṣasa warriors there.

sanskrit: hanyatāṃ dahyatāṃ vāpi bhakṣyatām iti cāpare rākṣasās tatra saṃkruddhāḥ parasparam athābruvan
english: "Let him be slain!" "Let him be burned!" "Let him be eaten!" — so the enraged rākṣasas there said to one another.

sanskrit: atītya mārgaṃ sahasā mahātmā sa tatra rakṣo'dhipapādamūle dadarśa rājñaḥ paricāravṛddhān gṛhaṃ mahāratnavibhūṣitaṃ ca
english: Swiftly traversing the path, that great-souled one arrived before the feet of the lord of rākṣasas and beheld there the senior attendants of the king and the palace adorned with great jewels.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ kapisattamam rakṣobhir vikṛtākāraiḥ kṛṣyamāṇam itas tataḥ
english: The immensely resplendent Rāvaṇa saw that foremost of monkeys being dragged hither and thither by rākṣasas of hideous forms.

sanskrit: rākṣasādhipatiṃ cāpi dadarśa kapisattamaḥ tejobalasamāyuktaṃ tapantam iva bhāskaram
english: And that foremost of monkeys also beheld the lord of rākṣasas, endowed with blazing power and strength, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: sa roṣasaṃvartitatāmradṛṣṭir daśānanas taṃ kapim anvavekṣya athopaviṣṭān kulaśīlavṛddhān samādiśat taṃ prati mantramukhyān
english: Ten-faced Rāvaṇa, his gaze reddened with swelling wrath, scrutinized the monkey and then directed the chief counselors seated there — elders distinguished by lineage, conduct, and age — regarding him.

sanskrit: yathākramaṃ taiḥ sa kapiś ca pṛṣṭaḥ kāryārtham arthasya ca mūlam ādau nivedayām āsa harīśvarasya dūtaḥ sakāśād aham āgato 'smi
english: Questioned by them in due order as to the purpose of his business and the root cause of the matter, the monkey announced at the outset: "I have come from the presence of Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, as his messenger."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa karmaṇā tasya vismito bhīmavikramaḥ hanumān roṣatāmrākṣo rakṣo'dhipam avaikṣata
english: Then Hanumān of terrible valor, astonished by his deeds, his eyes reddened with wrath, gazed upon the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: bhājamānaṃ mahārheṇa kāñcanena virājatā muktājālāvṛtenātha mukuṭena mahādyutim
english: He beheld him resplendent with a magnificent golden diadem wrapped in a net of pearls, of surpassing brilliance —

sanskrit: vajrasaṃyogasaṃyuktair mahārhamaṇivigrahaiḥ haimair ābharaṇaiś citrair manaseva prakalpitaiḥ
english: — adorned with golden ornaments of manifold kinds inset with highly precious gems set with diamonds, fashioned as if by the mind itself;

sanskrit: mahārhakṣaumasaṃvītaṃ raktacandanarūṣitam svanuliptaṃ vicitrābhir vividhabhiś ca bhaktibhiḥ
english: — clad in the most costly silk, smeared with red sandal paste, self-anointed, with varied and diverse decorative patterns;

sanskrit: vipulair darśanīyaiś ca rakṣākṣair bhīmadarśanaiḥ dīptatīkṣṇamahādaṃṣṭraiḥ pralambadaśanacchadaiḥ
english: — with broad, striking rākṣasa eyes terrible to behold, with blazing, sharp, and great fangs, and with hanging lips over the teeth;

sanskrit: śirobhir daśabhir vīraṃ bhrājamānaṃ mahaujasaḥ nānāvyālasamākīrṇaiḥ śikharair iva mandaram
english: — that hero gleaming with great splendor, with his ten heads, like Mount Mandara covered with various serpents at its peaks;

sanskrit: nīlāñjanacaya prakhyaṃ hāreṇorasi rājatā pūrṇacandrābhavaktreṇa sabalākam ivāmbudam
english: — dark as a heap of collyrium, his necklace gleaming on his chest, his face like the full moon, like a cloud attended by cranes;

sanskrit: bāhubhir baddhakeyūrair candanottamarūṣitaiḥ bhrājamānāṅgadaiḥ pīnaiḥ pañcaśīrṣair ivoragaiḥ
english: — his arms bound with armlets and smeared with the finest sandal paste, adorned with gleaming bracelets, massive, like five-headed serpents;

sanskrit: mahati sphāṭike citre ratnasaṃyogasaṃskṛte uttamāstaraṇāstīrṇe upaviṣṭaṃ varāsane
english: — seated on a great, jeweled, variegated crystal throne adorned with the finest gems, spread with the best of cushions;

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtābhir atyarthaṃ pramadābhiḥ samantataḥ vālavyajanahastābhir ārāt samupasevitam
english: — attended on all sides by exceedingly adorned ladies who held fly-whisks of yak-tail hair and served him from nearby;

sanskrit: durdhareṇa prahastena mahāpārśvena rakṣasā mantribhir mantratattvajñair nikumbhena ca mantriṇā
english: — accompanied by Durdhara, Prahasta, and the rākṣasa Mahāpārśva, by counselors versed in the true principles of counsel, and by the minister Nikumbha;

sanskrit: upopaviṣṭaṃ rakṣobhiś caturbhir baladarpitaiḥ kṛtsnaiḥ parivṛtaṃ lokaṃ caturbhir iva sāgaraiḥ
english: — flanked by four rākṣasas intoxicated with their strength, surrounding the entire world like the four oceans;

sanskrit: mantribhir mantratattvajñair anyaiś ca śubhabuddhibhiḥ anvāsyamānaṃ sacivaiḥ surair iva sureśvaram
english: — attended by counselors expert in the principles of statecraft and by others of auspicious intelligence, like the lord of gods attended by the gods;

sanskrit: apaśyad rākṣasapatiṃ hanūmān atitejasaṃ viṣṭhitaṃ meruśikhare satoyam iva toyadam
english: Hanumān beheld the lord of rākṣasas of immeasurable splendor, stationed there like a rain-laden cloud resting on the peak of Meru.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ saṃpīḍyamāno 'pi rakṣobhir bhīmavikramaiḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā rakṣo'dhipam avaikṣata
english: Though being pressed upon by those rākṣasas of terrible valor, he was filled with supreme amazement and gazed upon the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: bhrājamānaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā hanumān rākṣaseśvaram manasā cintayām āsa tejasā tasya mohitaḥ
english: Then Hanumān, seeing the lord of rākṣasas blazing in splendor, reflected in his mind, overwhelmed by his brilliance.

sanskrit: aho rūpam aho dhairyam aho sattvam aho dyutiḥ aho rākṣasarājasya sarvalakṣaṇayuktatā
english: "Ah, what form! Ah, what steadiness! Ah, what vigor! Ah, what radiance! Ah, how the king of rākṣasas is endowed with every auspicious mark!"

sanskrit: yady adharmo na balavān syād ayaṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ syād ayaṃ suralokasya saśakrasyāpi rakṣitā
english: "Were adharma not so powerful in him, this lord of rākṣasas would be the protector of the world of gods together with Indra himself."

sanskrit: tena bibhyati khalv asmāl lokāḥ sāmaradānavāḥ ayaṃ hy utsahate kruddhaḥ kartum ekārṇavaṃ jagat
english: "It is indeed from this one that the worlds tremble — gods, asuras, and all — for this one, when enraged, has the capacity to reduce the world to a single ocean."

sanskrit: iti cintāṃ bahuvidhām akaron matimān kapiḥ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasarājasya prabhāvam amitaujasaḥ
english: Thus the wise monkey turned over many such thoughts in his mind, having seen the power of the king of rākṣasas of immeasurable might.

sanskrit: tam udvīkṣya mahābāhuḥ piṅgākṣaṃ purataḥ sthitam roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭo rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ
english: Gazing up at him — that tawny-eyed one standing before him — Rāvaṇa the terror of the world, the long-armed one, was seized with great wrath.

sanskrit: sa rājā roṣatāmrākṣaḥ prahastaṃ mantrisattamam kālayuktam uvācedaṃ vaco vipulam arthavat
english: That king, his eyes reddened with anger, spoke this extensive and meaningful speech to Prahasta, the best of ministers, in words suited to the moment.

sanskrit: durātmā pṛcchyatām eṣa kutaḥ kiṃ vāsya kāraṇam vanabhaṅge ca ko 'syārtho rākṣasīnāṃ ca tarjane
english: "Let this wicked-souled one be questioned: where does he come from? What is his motive? What was his purpose in destroying the grove and in threatening the rākṣasī women?"

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahasto vākyam abravīt samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te na bhīḥ kāryā tvayā kape
english: Hearing Rāvaṇa's words, Prahasta spoke: "Take courage, all good to you; you need have no fear, O monkey."

sanskrit: yadi tāvat tvam indreṇa preṣito rāvaṇālayam tattvam ākhyāhi mā te bhūd bhayaṃ vānara mokṣyase
english: "If you have been sent by Indra to the abode of Rāvaṇa, tell the truth; let there be no fear for you, O monkey — you shall be released."

sanskrit: yadi vaiśravaṇasya tvaṃ yamasya varuṇasya ca cārurūpam idaṃ kṛtvā yamasya varuṇasya ca
english: "Or if you belong to Vaiśravaṇa, or to Yama, or to Varuṇa — having assumed this lovely form on behalf of Yama or Varuṇa —"

sanskrit: viṣṇunā preṣito vāpi dūto vijayakāṅkṣiṇā na hi te vānaraṃ tejo rūpamātraṃ tu vānaram
english: "— or if you have been sent as a messenger by Viṣṇu, who desires victory — for your brilliance is not that of a mere monkey; the form alone is a monkey's —"

sanskrit: tattvataḥ kathayasvādya tato vānara mokṣyase anṛtaṃ vadataś cāpi durlabhaṃ tava jīvitam
english: "— tell the truth now, and then, O monkey, you shall be released; but if you speak falsely, your life will be hard to preserve."

sanskrit: atha vā yannimittas te praveśo rāvaṇālaye
english: "Or else — whatever the cause of your entry into the abode of Rāvaṇa —"

sanskrit: evam ukto harivaras tadā rakṣogaṇeśvaram abravīn nāsmi śakrasya yamasya varuṇasya vā
english: Thus addressed, that best of monkeys then spoke to the lord of the rākṣasa host: "I am not of Śakra, nor of Yama, nor of Varuṇa —"

sanskrit: dhanadena na me sakhyaṃ viṣṇunā nāsmi coditaḥ jātir eva mama tv eṣā vānaro 'ham ihāgataḥ
english: "— I have no alliance with Dhanada, nor was I dispatched by Viṣṇu; this is simply my birth-nature — I am a monkey, and I have come here thus."

sanskrit: darśane rākṣasendrasya durlabhe tad idaṃ mayā vanaṃ rākṣasarājasya darśanārthe vināśitam
english: "Since an audience with the lord of rākṣasas is difficult to obtain, I destroyed this grove of the rākṣasa king for the purpose of obtaining that audience."

sanskrit: tatas te rākṣasāḥ prāptā balino yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ rakṣaṇārthaṃ ca dehasya pratiyuddhā mayā raṇe
english: "Then those powerful rākṣasas came, eager for battle; and for the protection of my body I fought back against them in combat."

sanskrit: astrapāśair na śakyo 'haṃ baddhuṃ devāsurair api pitāmahād eva varo mamāpy eṣo 'bhyupāgataḥ
english: "I cannot be bound by missile-fetters even by gods or asuras — this very boon has come to me as well from the Grandsire."

sanskrit: rājānaṃ draṣṭukāmena mayāstram anuvartitam vimukto aham astreṇa rākṣasais tv atipīḍitaḥ
english: "Desiring to see the king, I allowed the missile to have its effect; I was indeed freed from the missile, yet I was greatly tormented by the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: dūto 'ham iti vijñeyo rāghavasyāmitaujasaḥ śrūyatāṃ cāpi vacanaṃ mama pathyam idaṃ prabho
english: "I am to be understood as a messenger of Rāghava of immeasurable might; let this salutary message of mine be heard, O lord."
